elements.element: The aggregate liability cap applies mutually to both parties on the same basis.
elements.evidence: The added language caps “EACH PARTY'S TOTAL AGGREGATE LIABILITY” using the same formula.

elements.element: The fee-based limb of the cap includes both fees paid and fees payable.
elements.evidence: The clause uses “DEVELOPMENT COSTS ACTUALLY PAID OR INCURRED BY SFJ,” not fees paid or payable.

elements.element: The fee-based limb is measured over the 12 months preceding the claim.
elements.evidence: No 12-month lookback period or claim-based measurement date is included.

elements.element: The cap has a USD 1,000,000 floor.
elements.evidence: The second limb is “ONE MILLION U.S. DOLLARS ($1,000,000).”

elements.element: The cap is the greater of the applicable fee-based amount and USD 1,000,000.
elements.evidence: The cap expressly uses “THE GREATER OF” its first monetary limb and $1,000,000, although the first limb is substantively incorrect.

elements.element: Indirect damages are mutually excluded.
elements.evidence: The clause provides that “NEITHER PARTY” will be liable to the other for indirect damages.

elements.element: Consequential damages are mutually excluded.
elements.evidence: The clause provides that “NEITHER PARTY” will be liable to the other for consequential damages.

elements.element: Either party's breach of confidentiality obligations is carved out from the cap and uncapped.
elements.evidence: A party's breach of its confidentiality obligations is an “EXCLUDED CLAIM,” and Excluded Claims are excepted from each party's aggregate cap.

elements.element: Either party's breach of data protection obligations is carved out from the cap and uncapped.
elements.evidence: A party's breach of its data protection obligations is an “EXCLUDED CLAIM,” and Excluded Claims are excepted from the cap.

elements.element: Either party's breach of security obligations is carved out from the cap and uncapped.
elements.evidence: The definition mentions data protection but does not mention security obligations; these are separately required categories.

elements.element: Either party's indemnification obligations are carved out from the cap and uncapped.
elements.evidence: A party's indemnification obligations are expressly included in “EXCLUDED CLAIMS” and therefore excepted from the cap.

elements.element: Either party's gross negligence is carved out from the cap and uncapped.
elements.evidence: A party's gross negligence is expressly included in “EXCLUDED CLAIMS” and therefore excepted from the cap.

elements.element: Either party's wilful misconduct is carved out from the cap and uncapped.
elements.evidence: A party's wilful misconduct is expressly included in “EXCLUDED CLAIMS” and therefore excepted from the cap.

elements.element: Either party's fraud is carved out from the cap and uncapped.
elements.evidence: A party's fraud is expressly included in “EXCLUDED CLAIMS” and therefore excepted from the cap.

elements.element: Either party's infringement of the other party's intellectual property is carved out from the cap and uncapped.
elements.evidence: A party's infringement of the other party's intellectual property rights is expressly included in “EXCLUDED CLAIMS” and therefore excepted from the cap.

elements.element: Customer's payment obligations are not treated as damages for cap purposes.
elements.evidence: The clause merely excepts PB's payment obligations under Article 6 and Section 14.2. It neither states that payment obligations are not damages nor protects all of Customer's payment obligations.

elements.element: The aggregate liability cap applies mutually to both parties on the same basis.
elements.evidence: The added language applies the same aggregate cap formulation to “EACH PARTY.”

elements.element: The cap is based on fees.
elements.evidence: The cap is based on development costs actually paid or incurred by SFJ, not fees.

elements.element: The fee amount used for the cap covers 12 months.
elements.evidence: The clause contains no 12-month period.

elements.element: Either party's indemnification obligations are carved out from the cap and uncapped.
elements.evidence: Indemnification obligations are included in the mutual definition of “EXCLUDED CLAIMS” and excepted from the cap.

elements.evidence: Confidentiality breaches are included in the mutual definition of “EXCLUDED CLAIMS” and excepted from the cap.

result.reason: The operative language establishes a mutual aggregate cap, preserves the mutual damages exclusion, and includes most requested uncapped carve-outs. It does not satisfy either position because the cap is based on SFJ's development costs rather than fees and contains no 12-month lookback. The preferred position also fails because security obligations are omitted and only specified PB payments—not all Customer payment obligations—are excepted, without stating that such payments are not damages. The amendment does not contradict Section 14.4.2 or impair the specified Article 6 and Section 14.2 payment obligations, but it cannot be minimal because it reaches neither complete level.
